predicted_errors.error_location: Section on ELF-EMF (Burman et al., Sakhaie et al., Kim et al.) and Table 1 (rows for refs 143, 156)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: C57BL/6, C57BL/6NCrl, BALB/c and BALB/cAnNCrl are inbred MOUSE strains, yet they are repeatedly described as rats: 'Kim et al exposed male C57BL/6 adult rats', 'Sakhaie et al ... subject BALB/c rats', 'Burman et al ... exposing C57BL/6NCrl and BALB/cAnNCrl rats', and Table 1 lists 'C57BL/6 rats' and 'BALB/c rats'. The species of the experimental animals is misreported throughout, which also conflicts with the correct use of 'male LACA mice' elsewhere.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 'Effect of ELF-EMF exposure on brain tumor' (Ahlbom et al. pooled analysis)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states '99.2% of children residing in households with exposure levels below 0.4 μT exhibited a lower risk of developing childhood leukemia. In contrast, 0.8% of children exposed to 0.4 μT or higher displayed relatively elevated risk estimates'. In the original pooled analysis these percentages describe the DISTRIBUTION of children across exposure categories (99.2% below 0.4 μT, 0.8% at/above 0.4 μT), not the proportion of children showing lower/higher risk. Presenting an exposure-distribution statistic as a risk result is a misreading of the reported statistics.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 'Effect of ELF-EMF exposure on brain tumor' (first paragraph on childhood leukemia)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper first states 'The association between ELF-EMF exposure and cancer was first articulated in 1979 in the context of childhood leukemia.110' and in the very next sentence 'In 1976, Wertheimer and Leeper put forth a hypothesis ...110'. The two dates contradict each other while citing the same source; the landmark Wertheimer & Leeper study was published in 1979.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section on RF-EMR and brain development (migraine/benefit sentences, refs 74,90)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Two directly opposing claims are supported by the identical citation pair: 'In a recent study, the migraine reoccurrence rate in heavily exposed subjects increased.74,90 However, some studies have reported that exposure to RF-EMR improves cognitive activity and benefits CNS disorders.74,90'. The same references cannot simultaneously document increased migraine recurrence and cognitive benefit; at least one attribution is wrong.

'Several studies have indicated that there might be a link between RF-EMR and cancer,31,32 while contrasting studies have found no clear evidence of RF-EMR dormant carcinogenicity.32' Reference 32 is cited as evidence both for and against a carcinogenic link, indicating a citation/numbering error.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 'RF-EMR exposure effects on learning and memory'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Internally contradictory and unsupported assertions: 'RF-EMR exposure influences cognitive abilities, including memory loss and cognitive abilities in humans,58 and animals.59 But, there is no direct evidence for these effects.60' and the blanket statement 'Nonetheless, the RF-EMR exposure intensity in the public environment is not detrimental.53'. The latter categorical safety claim contradicts the paper's own stated conclusion that 'the precise conditions and circumstances under which detrimental or beneficial effects manifest ... remain uncertain'.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section on neurodegenerative disorders (Huss et al. statements)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text first asserts (Huss et al.) that 'residing in close proximity to power lines and experiencing residential ELF-EMF exposure might conceivably increase the risk of developing conditions such as ALS, PD, or multiple sclerosis (MS)', and two paragraphs later states 'After conducting a meta-analysis led by Huss et al, no compelling evidence supporting a relationship between exposure to ELF-EMF and an elevated risk of PD was identified.' The two attributions to the same author group are mutually contradictory for PD; moreover the cited power-line mortality study reported associations primarily for Alzheimer's/senile dementia rather than ALS/PD/MS.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 'Effect of ELF-EMF exposure on brain tumor' (Turner et al., refs 113, 118, 120)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Turner et al. are cited three times with mutually inconsistent conclusions: ref 113 ('occupational ELF-EMF exposure may promote glioma'), ref 118 ('did not yield conclusive evidence of associations between occupational ELF-EMF exposure and risk of glioma or meningioma'), and ref 120 (INTEROCC, 'positive correlation between exposure to ELF-EMF and the development of glioma'). Refs 113 and 120 appear to describe the same INTEROCC analysis twice, and the stated findings conflict with ref 118 without any reconciliation.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 'Effect of ELF-EMF exposure on brain tumor' (Mezei et al. meta-analysis)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The same paragraph states 'there was no compelling evidence to support an increased risk of childhood brain tumors associated with diverse exposure intensities' and then 'their findings did indicate a moderate risk increase for exposures exceeding 0.3 or 0.4 μT'. These are mutually inconsistent, and the cited meta-analysis concluded against an association, so the 'moderate risk increase' statement overstates the source.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 'RF-EMR exposure effects on the BBB' (Kuribayashi et al., ref 42)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: 'Kuribayashi et al did not witness BBB leakage during in vitro experiments.' The cited work on BBB permeability after 1439 MHz exposure was an in vivo study in immature and young rats, not an in vitro experiment; the study design is misdescribed.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section on ELF-EMF (Burman et al. description)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: 'exposing ... to the spectrum of 5-100 Hz electric field with a power of 8.56 V/m r.m.s (on-state) and 4.99 V/m r.m.s (off-state)'. V/m is a unit of electric field strength, not power; in addition, reporting a substantial field (4.99 V/m) for the 'off-state' sham condition is not explained and would undermine the sham control as described.

predicted_errors.error_location: Text (Kazemi et al., refs 141 and 142) vs Table 1 row for ref 157
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text describes the exposed animals as 'Wrhesus macaquesistar monkeys' / 'Wrhesus macaques/Star monkeys' (a corrupted species designation mixing 'Wistar' rats with rhesus macaques), while Table 1 lists the identical protocol (12 Hz, 0.7 μT, 4 h/d, 30 days) as performed in 'Rhesus macaque monkeys'. The species reported in the text is internally incoherent and inconsistent with the table.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section on RF-EMR and brain development (Belyaev et al.)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: 'Belyaev et al reported that 915 MHz RF-EMR exposure had adverse effects on human stem cells and could potentially cause cancer.' The cited work examined chromatin conformation/DNA repair foci in human stem cells; it did not demonstrate or conclude carcinogenicity, so the attributed conclusion overstates the source.
